## 6. Duplicate / related checks

For each orphan, checked whether its email or phone appears on **any**
`public.users` row (i.e. under a different ID). Read-only, matched on lowercased
email and on digits-only phone (`auth.users` stores phones without the `+`).

| # | Email | Email on another profile? | Phone on another profile? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | abdelrahman@bridgefi.me | **Yes** → profile `8d438c00…3467` (role `user`) | **Yes** → profile `8d438c00…3467` |
| 2 | omararafa7@gmail.com | No | n/a (no phone) |
| 3 | abdulrahmanredaa8@gmail.com | No | n/a (no phone) |

### What orphan #1 shows

This is a **two-sided inconsistency**, not a plain Auth-only orphan:

```text
public.users  8d438c00…3467   abdelrahman@bridgefi.me   created 2026-08-16   ← no auth user
auth.users    b7dcf7b0…b5e3   abdelrahman@bridgefi.me   created 2026-09-01   ← no profile
```

Two different IDs hold the same email address, one on each side of the boundary.

**Fact:** `public.users.email` carries a `UNIQUE` constraint
(`users_email_unique`, `0000_init.sql:79`). A signup for this address therefore
*cannot* insert a profile row while `8d438c00…3467` exists — the insert fails
with SQLSTATE `23505`, which under the pre-fix code returned HTTP 500 and left
the newly created Auth user behind. The state above is exactly what that failure
produces.

**Assumption, not verified:** that the original Auth user for profile
`8d438c00…3467` was deleted at some point (dashboard or script), which is what
would have freed the address on the Auth side and allowed `b7dcf7b0…b5e3` to be
created. The Auth audit log would confirm or refute this.

**Consequence for cleanup:** orphan #1 cannot be resolved by deleting the Auth
user alone. Whoever performs the cleanup must decide what happens to the
surviving profile row `8d438c00…3467` and any data cascading from it. Orphans #2
and #3 have no such entanglement.

## 7. Application impact (verified against the code)

**Verified — an Auth user with no profile row is rejected.**
[`apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts`](apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts) validates the
Bearer token with `supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token)` (line 27), then loads the
profile:

```ts
const [row] = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, data.user.id)).limit(1);
if (!row) {
  return errorResponse(c, 'unauthorized', 'User profile not found');   // line 34
}
```

So a token belonging to an orphan is cryptographically valid but every protected
endpoint answers **401 `User profile not found`**.

**Verified — the role these users would need lives only in the missing row.**
`requireAuth` puts the profile row on the context (lines 37–38);
[`requireAdmin`](apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts#L12) and
[`requireLabPartner`](apps/api/src/middleware/lab-partner.ts#L12) then compare
`user.role`, and clients receive it via `serializeUser`
([`serialize.ts:72`](apps/api/src/lib/serialize.ts#L72)) on `GET /users/me`.
Nothing reads `user_metadata`, `app_metadata`, or JWT claims for authorization.
No profile row therefore means **no role at all**, not a default one.

**Verified — the resulting user-visible loop.** `POST /auth/login`
([`routes/auth.ts`](apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts)) only touches `auth.users`, so an
orphan **can** sign in and receive a token — which is why all three orphans have a
populated `last_sign_in_at`. The very next call, `GET /users/me`, then 401s; the
web client treats a 401 on an authenticated request as a dead session, clears it,
and bounces to `/login` ([`apps/web/lib/api.ts:201-204`](apps/web/lib/api.ts#L201-L204)).
The user can log in and is immediately logged out again, indefinitely.

**Verified — the address stays occupied.** `auth.users` owns email uniqueness and
has no foreign key to `public.users` (`0000_init.sql:65-80` defines no FK; the
same is documented in [`reset-dev-users.ts:10-14`](apps/api/src/db/reset-dev-users.ts#L10-L14)).
A retry with the same address hits `email_exists` on
`auth.admin.createUser` and returns 409 "email already exists". Deleting the
profile row would not help; for orphan #1 there is no profile row to delete.

**Current practical state (fact, from §4):** with `matched = 0`, no account in
this project can currently use any authenticated endpoint of the API.

**Scope note:** the signup route was fixed earlier today so that a failed profile
insert now rolls the Auth user back. That fix prevents *new* orphans. It does
nothing to the three records above.

## 9. Method — how this report was produced

### Attempt 1 — direct SQL (not used)

A single read-only SQL join was attempted first over `DATABASE_URL`, inside an
explicit `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` transaction. It could not connect:

```text
28P01  password authentication failed for user "postgres"
```

The connection string's **shape is correct** — user `postgres.<project-ref>`,
host `aws-1-eu-central-1.pooler.supabase.com`, port `6543` (transaction pooler),
`sslmode=require`, matching the documented format in `apps/api/.env.example`. The
**password in the local `apps/api/.env` is stale** (that file dates from
2026-06-27). Nothing was changed to work around this; no credential was rotated,
and the production value on Render was neither read nor modified.

The query that *would* have been run, for the record — SELECT only:

```sql
-- Totals
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM auth.users)   AS auth_total,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.users) AS app_total;

-- Orphans: auth.users with no profile of the same id
SELECT a.id, a.email, a.created_at, a.email_confirmed_at, a.phone, a.last_sign_in_at
FROM auth.users a
LEFT JOIN public.users u ON u.id = a.id
WHERE u.id IS NULL
ORDER BY a.created_at ASC;
```

### Attempt 2 — read-only HTTP (used for every number in this report)

Fell back to the same auth-side path `reset-dev-users.ts` already uses, which
reads Auth through the Admin API rather than SQL:

| Data | Call | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `auth.users` | `supabase.auth.admin.listUsers({ page, perPage: 1000 })` | GET `/auth/v1/admin/users` |
| `public.users` | `supabase.from('users').select('id,email,phone,role,created_at')` | GET `/rest/v1/users` |
| count check | `supabase.from('users').select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })` | HEAD `/rest/v1/users` |

The join was then computed in memory **on `id`**. Email and phone were compared
only for the §6 collision check, never to establish orphan status.

**Read-only guarantees:** GET/HEAD requests exclusively. No `DELETE`, `INSERT`,
`UPDATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `CREATE`, `GRANT`, or `REVOKE` was issued.
No `deleteUser`, `updateUserById`, or `inviteUserByEmail` call exists in the
scripts. No migration, no `drizzle-kit push`/`migrate`, and
`reset-dev-users.ts` was never executed.

**Execution.** `pnpm` is not installed on the machine this ran from, so the
package scripts could not be used. Two throwaway ES-module scripts were run
directly with Node 24 against the pre-existing `node_modules`, resolving
`@supabase/supabase-js` and `dotenv` from the workspace root:

```bash
node orphan-audit.tmp.mjs      # main audit  → JSON
node orphan-verify.tmp.mjs     # exact-count cross-check
```

Both scripts read `apps/api/.env` at runtime, printed no secrets, and **were
deleted immediately after this report was written**. Neither is part of the
codebase.

### Caveats on the numbers

- **Two snapshots, not one.** Because SQL was unavailable, `auth.users` and
  `public.users` were read seconds apart via separate HTTP calls rather than in
  one transactional snapshot. With 3 and 1 rows and no signup traffic during the
  read, the risk of skew is negligible — but the reads were not atomic.
- **Totals independently verified.** The `public.users` total came from a
  PostgREST `count=exact` request (1) and the Auth total from the Admin API's own
  reported total (3), so neither figure depends on the pagination loop.
- **Project identity is an assumption.** Project ref `uwoxelinwwhdocckulvl` comes
  from the local `apps/api/.env` and matches the committed `.env.example`. The
  Render service's own environment variables were not read (they are not in the
  repo and reading them was out of scope), so *this is the project the repository
  is configured against*, which is not the same statement as *this is the project
  production is pointed at*. The service-role key authenticated successfully, so
  the project is live and the key is current.

## 9b. ADDENDUM — 2026-09-04, application-data reconciliation

Added after the auth-system rebuild. Same read-only method as §9 (Auth Admin
API + PostgREST `GET`, `count=exact`). **Nothing was deleted, inserted, or
updated.** No user from §2 was removed.

### Every user-referencing table is empty

All 12 tables that point at a user hold **zero rows**:

```text
subscriptions            0     ai_chat_summaries     0
user_biomarker_results   0     notifications         0
lab_uploads              0     device_tokens         0
score_snapshots          0     bookings              0
ai_chat_messages         0     addon_orders          0
ai_insights              0     lab_partner_areas     0
```

Seed and reference data is intact and untouched: 94 biomarkers, 8 biomarker
categories, 2 subscription plans, 1 service area, 15 availability windows, 8
health goals, 6 interventions, 4 notification templates, 3 app settings.

### Consequence

**No customer or clinical data exists anywhere in this project.** Not one
booking, subscription, biomarker result, lab upload, AI conversation,
notification, device token, or score snapshot is attached to any of the three
orphaned identities or to the one profile. The profile is named
"AbdulRahman **Test**".

So the two questions §15 asks about each record answer themselves:

| Record | Related application records | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Auth `b7dcf7b0…` abdelrahman@bridgefi.me | none | split identity, see below |
| Auth `c2c77a6d…` omararafa7@gmail.com | none | no `full_name` metadata |
| Auth `0995a27e…` abdulrahmanredaa8@gmail.com | none | no `full_name` metadata |
| Profile `8d438c00…` abdelrahman@bridgefi.me, role `user` | none | "AbdulRahman Test", created 2026-08-16 |

Also checked and clean: no duplicate profile emails, no duplicate profile
phones, no role values outside `(user, admin, lab_partner)`, and no application
row referencing a missing user.

### Resolution path — still no deletion required

The rebuild made deletion unnecessary rather than merely deferred:

- **`c2c77a6d…` and `0995a27e…`** self-heal. Signup now provisions the missing
  profile for an identity whose password the requester proves, so either of
  these becomes a working account the next time its owner submits signup with
  the same email and password. No operator action, no data loss.
- **`b7dcf7b0…` cannot self-heal** — profile `8d438c00…` holds the address
  under a different id, so the insert would violate `users_email_unique`.
  Signup returns a 409 pointing at support, and `db:check-users` lists it under
  SPLIT IDENTITIES.

### Recommendation for the split identity (not executed)

Deleting profile `8d438c00…` would let Auth identity `b7dcf7b0…` self-heal, and
because that profile has **zero** related records in all 12 tables, nothing
would be lost but the string "AbdulRahman Test". That is still a deletion of a
row in the production project, so it is **not performed here**. It needs your
explicit go-ahead, and the alternative — `db:ensure-admin` provisioning a fresh
profile under a different address — avoids the deletion entirely.

The IDs must **not** be merged: `auth.id != profile.id` is the whole problem,
and rewriting either id would be a silent data mutation.

### On a clean reset

The evidence would permit one under §16 of the rebuild brief: no customer data,
one test profile, three identities created during the debugging window. It was
**not done**, because it is unnecessary — the self-healing path plus one
operator decision reaches the same end state without destroying anything, and
two of the three addresses are external `@gmail.com` accounts that may belong to
real people. Resetting merely because cleanup is easier is exactly what the
brief rules out.
